name: How can framing help soundproof a basement ceiling?

mainEntity.name: How can framing help soundproof a basement ceiling?

acceptedAnswer.text: To block footstep noise and upstairs voices, you can frame the basement ceiling using resilient channels or sound isolation clips instead of screwing drywall directly to joists. Installing mineral wool sound insulation batts between the joist bays prior to boarding also absorbs significant airborne sound. If high-level sound isolation is the goal, trade off a couple of inches of ceiling height by constructing an independent, free-standing ceiling joist grid decoupled entirely from the subfloor above.
acceptedAnswer.description: Using sound clips, resilient channel, dense insulation batts, or decoupled joists isolates sound vibration between floors.
